actives.name: Salicylic Acid (BHA)
actives.scientific_basis: Lipid-soluble beta-hydroxy acid that penetrates into pilosebaceous units to dissolve intercellular desmosomes and sebum plugs, preventing microcomedone formation.

evidence.title: Guidelines of care for the management of acne vulgaris.

actives.name: Topical Retinoids (Adapalene)
actives.scientific_basis: Consensus first-line treatment for comedonal acne. Binds nuclear retinoic acid receptors (RAR-beta/gamma) to normalize follicular desquamation and increase cell turnover.

evidence.title: Topical retinoids in acne - an evidence-based overview.

actives.name: Glycolic Acid (AHA)
actives.scientific_basis: Alpha-hydroxy acid that exfoliates the stratum corneum by decreasing corneocyte cohesion, aiding comedone clearance and improving skin texture.

evidence.title: Glycolic acid peel therapy – a current review.

actives.name: Benzoyl Peroxide (BPO)
actives.scientific_basis: Generates free radicals/singlet oxygen within follicles, rapidly reducing Cutibacterium acnes load without inducing bacterial resistance.

evidence.title: Benzoyl peroxide: a review of its mechanism of action and clinical efficacy.

actives.name: Niacinamide (Topical)
actives.scientific_basis: Potent anti-inflammatory agent that inhibits IL-8 and neutrophil chemotaxis induced by C. acnes while suppressing cutaneous sebum synthesis.

evidence.title: Topical 4% niacinamide vs. 1% clindamycin in moderate inflammatory acne.

actives.name: Clindamycin + BPO Combination
actives.scientific_basis: Synergistic antimicrobial action combining lincosamide protein synthesis inhibition with oxidative bactericidal effect to suppress papular flare-ups.

evidence.title: Treatment of acne with a combination clindamycin/benzoyl peroxide gel.

actives.name: Benzoyl Peroxide (BPO)
actives.scientific_basis: Rapid bactericidal agent against C. acnes in pus-filled lesions, effectively clearing follicular oxidative microenvironments.

evidence.title: Benzoyl peroxide: mechanism of action and clinical efficacy.

actives.name: Dapsone (Topical Gel)
actives.scientific_basis: Sulfone compound with direct anti-inflammatory action by suppressing reactive oxygen species generation from polymorphonuclear leukocytes in pustular lesions.

evidence.title: Once-daily dapsone gel 7.5% for treatment of acne vulgaris.

actives.name: Zinc PCA / Topical Zinc
actives.scientific_basis: Inhibits 5-alpha reductase activity to lower sebum output and suppresses C. acnes lipases and inflammatory cytokine cascades.

evidence.title: Multicenter randomized comparative double-blind study evaluating topical zinc versus erythromycin in acne.

actives.name: Azelaic Acid
actives.scientific_basis: Reversible competitive inhibitor of tyrosinase that selectively targets hyperactive, abnormal melanocytes to diminish post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH).

evidence.title: Azelaic acid: review of pharmacological properties and therapeutic efficacy.

actives.name: Tranexamic Acid
actives.scientific_basis: Inhibits plasminogen activator system and reduces melanocyte-keratinocyte interactions triggered by UV and inflammatory mediators.

evidence.title: Tranexamic acid in dark spot and post-inflammatory pigmentation management.

actives.name: L-Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C)
actives.scientific_basis: Potent antioxidant that interacts with copper ions at tyrosinase active site to inhibit melanin production while scavenging free radicals.

evidence.title: Vitamin C in dermatology.

actives.name: Dermatologist Referral (Systemic Isotretinoin)
actives.scientific_basis: First-line oral retinoid therapy addressing all 4 key acne pathogenic pathways: sebocyte apoptosis, follicular hyperkeratosis normalization, C. acnes suppression, and profound anti-inflammatory action.

evidence.title: The use of isotretinoin in the treatment of acne vulgaris.

actives.name: Spironolactone (Oral Anti-Androgen)
actives.scientific_basis: Blocks androgen receptors and inhibits 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, effective for female hormonal deep nodular acne around the lower face.

evidence.title: Spironolactone for the treatment of acne in adult females.

actives.name: Centella Asiatica / Madecassoside
actives.scientific_basis: Promotes microvascular repair, enhances collagen synthesis, and suppresses vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) hyper-reactivity following acute cutaneous inflammation.

evidence.title: Centella asiatica in dermatology: an overview.

actives.name: Niacinamide (Topical)
actives.scientific_basis: Strengthens microvascular integrity and suppresses inflammatory signaling molecules (IL-6, TNF-alpha) causing persistent post-lesional macular redness.

evidence.title: The effect of niacinamide on reducing cutaneous pigmentation and erythema.

actives.name: Zinc PCA
actives.scientific_basis: Regulates sebocyte lipid synthesis by inhibiting 5-alpha reductase activity and reducing sebum secretion rate without causing epidermal dehydration.

evidence.title: Facial seborrhea and sebum excretion control by topical zinc.

actives.name: Green Tea Extract (EGCG)
actives.scientific_basis: Epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) targets IGF-1 signaling pathways in human sebocytes, modulating lipid production and reducing C. acnes inflammation.

evidence.title: Epigallocatechin-3-gallate improves acne in a randomized controlled trial.

actives.name: Ceramide Complex (1:3:1 ratio)
actives.scientific_basis: Replenishes intracellular lipid matrix of stratum corneum, restoring trans-epidermal water loss (TEWL) protection during active acne therapy.

evidence.title: The role of ceramides in skin barrier repair and acne management.

actives.name: Panthenol (Vitamin B5)
actives.scientific_basis: Acts as a humectant and epithelization precursor, accelerating barrier re-epithelialization and calming cutaneous irritation.

evidence.title: Skin moisturizing effects of panthenol-based formulations.

chin_jawline_inflammatory.name: Hormonal Distribution Pattern
chin_jawline_inflammatory.description: High concentration of inflammatory papules/nodules localized on the chin and jawline strongly correlates with endocrine/androgen-mediated sebaceous gland hypersensitivity.
chin_jawline_inflammatory.clinical_recommendation: Consider systemic anti-androgen evaluation (e.g. Spironolactone) or topical androgen receptor inhibitor alongside topical retinoids.

tzone_comedones.name: Seborrheic T-Zone Pattern
tzone_comedones.description: Dense comedonal clustering on forehead and nose correlates with high regional sebaceous gland density and hyperkeratinization.
tzone_comedones.clinical_recommendation: Prioritize lipophilic keratolytic actives (Salicylic Acid 2%) combined with Zinc PCA to control sebum rate.

cheek_friction_barrier.name: Cheek Barrier Compromise Pattern
cheek_friction_barrier.description: Localized inflammatory lesions on mid-cheeks frequently correlate with external friction (e.g., phone contact, pillowcases) and localized stratum corneum barrier disruption.
cheek_friction_barrier.clinical_recommendation: Integrate ceramide-rich barrier repair alongside gentle non-irritating antimicrobials.

synergies.name: Epiduo Synergy Protocol
synergies.description: Combining adapalene (keratolytic/anti-inflammatory) with benzoyl peroxide (bactericidal) provides superior clinical efficacy over monotherapy by targeting multiple pathogenic pathways simultaneously.
synergies.usage: Use BPO in AM routine and Adapalene in PM routine to minimize irritation while maintaining peak efficacy.

synergies.name: Pore Clearance & Barrier Shield Synergy
synergies.description: Salicylic acid unclogs follicular pores while Niacinamide strengthens stratum corneum lipids and lowers sebum production.
synergies.usage: Apply Niacinamide serum followed by BHA treatment.

synergies.name: Dual-Action Pigment & Erythema Defense
synergies.description: Azelaic acid inhibits tyrosinase while Niacinamide inhibits melanosome transfer, providing synergistic fading of post-acne dark marks.
synergies.usage: Layer Niacinamide before Azelaic acid application in morning routine.

conflicts.name: Exfoliation Overload Risk
conflicts.description: Simultaneous application of high-potency retinoids and leave-on BHAs can compromise the skin barrier and cause excessive desquamation, erythema, and dryness.
conflicts.resolution: Alternate nights: Use Retinoid on Night A, BHA Exfoliant on Night B.

conflicts.name: Co-Application Irritation Rule
conflicts.description: Applying unformulated retinoids and benzoyl peroxide at the exact same moment may trigger skin stinging. (Note: fixed-dose combination formulations handle this via chemical stabilization).
conflicts.resolution: Split timing: Benzoyl Peroxide in Morning (AM), Retinoid at Night (PM).
